value.name: Silicon Valley Clean Energy (SVCE)
value.notes: SVCE's own 'The Agency' page confirms Sunnyvale as one of 13 member jurisdictions. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Sunnyvale/Santa Clara County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value: Only one inspection is required for small residential rooftop solar energy systems eligible for expedited review, which may include a consolidated inspection by the building official and fire chief

value.notes: The City's own SolarApp+ for Solar Installers page states 'Eligible contractors can use SolarAPP+ for instantaneous rooftop solar permitting in the City of Sunnyvale.'

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited streamlined solar permitting (AB 2188, Civil Code Section 714, Government Code Section 65850.5 compliant)
other_conditions: Expedited process applies to single- or duplex-family dwellings with arrays not exceeding the maximum legal building height
Larger rooftop systems (10kW and above) require standard building and electrical permits with full plan review
No building permit shall be issued for construction that would interfere with solar access to rooftops of permitted structures on adjacent properties or preexisting active solar systems

sources.title: Chapter 16.66: Expedited Permit Process for Small Rooftop Solar Systems
